{{Short description|Class satisfying a generalization of Ramsey's theorem}}

In the area of mathematics known as [[Ramsey theory]], a '''Ramsey class'''<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nešetřil |first1=Jaroslav |title=All the Ramsey Classes - צילום הרצאות סטודיו האנה בי - YouTube |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=_pfa5bogr8g |website=www.youtube.com |publisher=Tel Aviv University |accessdate=4 November 2020 |date=2016-06-14}}</ref> is one which satisfies a generalization of [[Ramsey's theorem]].

Suppose <math>A</math>, <math>B</math> and <math>C</math> are structures and <math>k</math> is a positive integer. We denote by <math>\binom{B}{A}</math> the set of all subobjects <math>A'</math> of <math>B</math> which are isomorphic to <math>A</math>. We further denote by <math>C \rightarrow (B)^A_k</math> the property that for all partitions <math>X_1 \cup X_2\cup \dots\cup X_k</math> of <math>\binom{C}{A}</math> there exists a <math>B' \in \binom{C}{B}</math> and an <math>1 \leq i \leq k</math> such that <math>\binom{B'}{A} \subseteq X_i</math>.

Suppose <math>K</math> is a class of structures closed under [[isomorphism]] and [[substructure (mathematics)|substructures]]. We say the class <math>K</math> has the '''A-Ramsey property''' if for ever positive integer <math>k</math> and for every <math>B\in K</math> there is a <math>C \in K</math> such that <math>C \rightarrow (B)^A_k</math> holds. If <math>K</math> has the <math>A</math>-Ramsey property for all <math>A \in K</math> then we say <math>K</math> is a '''Ramsey class'''.

Ramsey's theorem is equivalent to the statement that the class of all finite sets is a Ramsey class.

<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Bodirsky |first1=Manuel |title=Ramsey Classes: Examples and Constructions |date=27 May 2015 |class=math.CO |eprint=1502.05146}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hubička |first1=Jan |last2=Nešetřil |first2=Jaroslav | authorlink2=Jaroslav Nešetřil |title=All those Ramsey classes (Ramsey classes with closures and forbidden homomorphisms) |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |date=November 2019 |volume=356 |article-number=106791 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2019.106791 |arxiv=1606.07979|s2cid=7750570 }}</ref>
